role: AI Systems Performance Engineer - New Graduate
key_responsibilities: Bring up foundation models (LLMs/multimodal) on the SambaNova stack
Profile model execution, find bottlenecks across model/compiler/runtime/hardware
Optimize AI workloads for throughput, latency, memory efficiency, scalability
Explore quantization, scheduling, caching, memory optimization
Develop tools, benchmarks, perf analysis for large-scale inference
Contribute dataflow/scheduling/system optimizations for single-node and distributed inference

strengths: CUDA kernel optimization (VGG16 project: memory coalescing, constant memory, ~35% speedup, profiling) - direct hit on GPU programming + memory hierarchy + perf optimization
SLM quantization + benchmarking (8-bit LLM.int8, pynvml VRAM/latency profiling, HellaSwag/GSM8K/ARC) - direct hit on quantization + model inference + benchmarks
GPT-2 + ASR transformers from scratch (multi-head attention, custom tokenizers) - direct hit on transformer architectures
TensorRT-optimized YOLO in COFFIN (5.2x speedup) - direct hit on inference optimization + TensorRT
MPI/SLURM HPC projects (10.49x, 30x speedups, load-imbalance/scaling analysis) - direct hit on parallel computing + HPC + scheduling
real_gaps: No vLLM/DeepSpeed/Megatron; TensorRT is the only serving-framework overlap
Distributed *model inference* (tensor/pipeline parallelism for one model across nodes) not shown - MPI work is distributed compute, different thing
KV cache / continuous batching not explicitly implemented (attention built from scratch, but no inference-time cache)
No experience with reconfigurable dataflow / non-GPU accelerators (SambaNova's specific hardware - learn on job)
overstated_by_keywords: 'distributed execution' - keyword matches MPI, but JD means distributed LLM inference, which is a genuine gap
'multimodal models' - DONUT is a document VLM (reasonably adjacent) but not frontier multimodal LLMs
llm_analysis.reasoning: This role's preferred-qualifications list reads almost like Justin's project portfolio: CUDA kernel optimization, quantization, transformer internals, profiling, and HPC/parallelism are all backed by concrete metric-bearing projects, and every basic qualification is met. The real gaps are serving-stack specific (vLLM/Megatron, KV-cache/batching, distributed model inference) and the SambaNova-specific dataflow hardware, all of which the JD frames as learn-on-the-job for a new grad. The only non-technical risk is sponsorship, which the posting does not address.
